1.table_content: Randomized two-condition lab experiment, N = 200 (98 women, 102 men), one participant per session. Two postures from Carney et al., held 3 min each. Outcomes: salivary testosterone and cortisol (before and about 17 min after), proportion of risky choices (6 gain, 6 loss, 50/50 gambles), tournament choice, 4-point self-reported power. Two-tailed t tests. Population, site, dates, postures, stakes and item wording not stated in the main text
1.verification_state: FULL-TEXT-CONFIRMED (main text). Supplement-dependent details are PROVISIONAL (not attached)

2.table_content: Title: "No Effect on Hormones and Risk Tolerance…". Body: "no significant effect", "failed to confirm". Discussion: effects "certainly plausible" under specific conditions; "more research is needed"

3.table_content: In this protocol and sample, self-reported power was higher (d = 0.344). No significant difference in testosterone change, cortisol or gain-domain risk (CIs as reported). Other tasks not significant

4.table_content: None retrieved. Limitation is NO RETRIEVAL CAPABILITY, not absence of use

5A.table_content: "no significant impact" / "failed to confirm" → title "No Effect" (also once in Results, for cortisol). Secondary: two analytes → "Hormones". PAPER

6.table_content: Testosterone-change null as quantified in Results
6.verification_state: FULL-TEXT-CONFIRMED that the source states it. Statistics not recomputed; OSF data not accessed

scope: Scope: whether the numbers a source reports for one two-sample t test agree with each other at their reported precision, and whether a claim restates them faithfully. It does not reanalyse data, judge the analysis, or say whether a non-significant result shows the absence of an effect.
